title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

errors: Too illegible and too heavily crossed out to verify any precise statement.

The claim that the adelic group is 'indépendant de ξ' cannot be checked as stated. In the modern description the inner form at p (and the global group I) depends on whether ξ is ordinary or supersingular, while the prime-to-p part is indeed independent.

ideas.what: Describing pairs (elliptic curve, level structure) in an isogeny class as a torsor under an adelic group with local factors: prime-to-p Tate module, a p-adic Frobenius/Dieudonné factor, and an archimedean factor
ideas.modern_name: Adelic description of isogeny classes / Langlands–Rapoport-type description of mod-p points of modular curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1960s, congruence relations for modular curves), Shimura, later Langlands–Rapoport (1987) and Kottwitz (1992)

ideas.what: Using Deuring's reduction/lifting theory of CM elliptic curves to produce a canonical element (Frobenius as an element of an imaginary quadratic field) attached to the curve mod p
ideas.modern_name: Deuring lifting; Frobenius as a Weil number; Honda–Tate for elliptic curves

ideas.what: An adelic group/gerbe whose p-component is defined by Frobenius-semilinear (Dieudonné-type) data and whose other components are ℓ-adic and archimedean realizations, as part of a 'Galois theory of motives'
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois gerbe over finite fields with local fibre functors (Langlands–Rapoport pseudomotivic groupoid, Milne's motivic gerbes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck appears to be organising elliptic curves over finite fields (with level structure) via an adelic group combining prime-to-p Tate modules, a p-adic Frobenius component and an archimedean component, singling out a 'Deuring element' ξ_p. This is a motivic-Galois-flavoured precursor of the Langlands–Rapoport groupoid picture, written in the context of his 'Galois theory of motives'.
missed.quote: sur l'anneau des adèles ... sur A''=A'×A_∞ ... et qui sur A_p est ... Tout ceci posé, la théorie de Hasse-Weil nous fournit a) un élément ξ_p ∈ 𝒯_p (l'élément de Deuring)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If the dating to the 1960s holds, this would be an early, independent instance of the adelic, place-by-place gerbe viewpoint on motives over finite fields, predating Langlands–Rapoport. It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty, since Ihara had similar ideas for modular curves.

deep.surprise_reason: The page seems to contain an adelic, Deuring-based description of isogeny classes of elliptic curves in a motivic-Galois framework. Historically interesting as an unpublished precursor of Langlands–Rapoport-style pictures. However, it is fragmentary, mostly illegible and crossed out, and the mathematics overlaps known work of Ihara, Shimura and Deuring.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads 'Donc on peut identifier les (C,α) [entre eux], en termes des [C(ξ), α(ξ)] canoniques'. The interlinear word above 'considérer' is 'identifier'.
The boxed crossed-out passage concerns 'A'' = A'×A_∞ (anneau des adèles premiers à p)', not 'adèles de groupes'.
'Tout ceci posé, la théorie de Hasse-Weil nous fournit' is followed by 'd'abord' (?) and then items a) and b).
Margin note at the left near the bottom-middle is crossed out (possibly 'Astérisque'/'à reprendre'); illegible.
Item b) seems to read 'une section ... unique au signe près à l'infini' and '... valeurs en p ... et la valeur en ∞ est la valuation dominée par T'. These are uncertain readings.
The neighbouring pages are typed pages from an unrelated analytic-functions draft (numbered 21 and 13), not continuations of this sheet.
